Subject: Single-conversation omission request (RID-SOL-9327)

Hi Aisha,

Following up from our call — we need Redwood to remove a single conversation (internal logs and audit exports) tied to RID-SOL-9327. This is a patient-related thread that mistakenly got ingested; the customer has provided a signed authorization (attached) and a short legal note. We only want one thread removed, not the account or broader dataset. Can you confirm the exact information you need from us and the expected timeline?

On Fri, 28 Aug 2026 at 15:05, Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com> wrote:
To: Natalie Green <natalie.green@acmehealth.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 28 Aug 2026 15:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Single-conversation omission request (RID-SOL-9327)

Hi Natalie — thanks for sending this over and for the attachment.

Short answer: we can remove a single conversation from our internal logs and from any generated audit exports that haven't been archived to an immutable store. To proceed we need:
- Exact thread identifier as recorded in your request (you listed RID-SOL-9327; if there are alternate IDs from your side please include)
- A signed authorization from the data subject or authorized legal representative (we have the PDF you attached)
- Confirmation that you only want this one thread removed and acknowledgement of the record we will keep for our deletion audit (we keep a redaction record referencing the request id; it does not include message contents)

Operationally, once we receive confirmation we will:
1) Quarantine the conversation and take a snapshots-of-record for our internal deletion verification (this snapshot is encrypted and stored only for the compliance window)
2) Remove the messages from live audit indexes, aggregated logs, and any active exports within 48–72 hours (longer if the conversation is present in an immutable 3rd-party backup)
3) Provide you with a deletion confirmation package (audit-excerpt-RID-SOL-9327.txt) with timestamps and the actions taken

I'll loop in Security & Legal to validate scope and to keep a record.

Best,
Aisha Rahman
Account Lead, Compliance Escalations
Redwood Inference

2) A CISO-approved contact at Acme who can sign off on cross-service deletions (email is fine).

If both are present, Security can proceed with emergency omission and we'll produce the audit excerpt for Acme. If the thread has been exported to a third-party analytics partner, removal may require coordination with them — I'll mark this P1 and flag for procurement if needed.
